chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'But do not promise them secretly in a subtle way.' He said, 'The man says, I promise you my father's house,' hinting to her with modesty and setting a time.
Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said: 'Except that you say a good word.'
And the good word is hinting at proposal in a proper manner and its ruling. 'And do not resolve upon the marriage contract until the term expires.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between 'promising secretly' and 'a good word' in Quranic courtship rulings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the nuances of courtship during the waiting period (*Iddah*), distinguishing between 'secret promise' (*wa'id sirran*)—which implies modest hinting at marriage rather than explicit commitment—and 'good words' (*qawl ma'ruf*), which denotes proper proposal etiquette. He clarifies that the prohibition against finalizing the marriage contract (*'azm al-'aqd*) until the expiration of the waiting period serves to prevent premature binding while allowing for the preliminary stages of courtship.
